tagline: Escalate Stripe billing failures into Jira tickets with revenue context
metaTitle: Jira + Stripe Integration: Payment Failure Incidents
metaDescription: Catch billing bugs before they cost revenue. GAIA opens a Jira incident when Stripe payment failures spike and notes the revenue at risk. See the setup steps.
intro:
For enterprise SaaS companies, Stripe is the revenue engine and Jira is the engineering command center. When Stripe reports payment failures, webhook errors, or subscription anomalies, those events require immediate engineering investigation — but the path from a dashboard alert to a properly filed, prioritized ticket is rarely automated.

GAIA connects the two so revenue-critical events automatically generate engineering tickets with the context needed for fast resolution. Payment failure spikes create urgent bugs with error codes and affected plan data. Webhook delivery failures become tasks with replay instructions. API deprecation notices create tickets with deadlines and code references. Engineers prioritize billing work with full revenue impact data visible in the Jira issue.

For companies where billing reliability is a board-level metric, billing anomalies never wait in someone's inbox before reaching the engineering team.

useCases.title: Payment failure spike to Jira incident ticket
useCases.description: When Stripe reports a spike in payment failures above your configured threshold, GAIA creates a Blocker-priority incident ticket with the failure rate, error codes, affected plan types, and estimated MRR impact.

useCases.title: Revenue impact annotation on billing tickets
useCases.description: GAIA enriches billing-related tickets with live revenue data, MRR at risk, number of affected subscriptions, and churn probability, so engineering can prioritize by financial impact.

useCases.title: Webhook failure tracking
useCases.description: When webhook delivery fails for a critical event type, GAIA creates a task with the event ID, endpoint URL, failure reason, and instructions for replaying the event.

useCases.title: Stripe API deprecation management
useCases.description: When API version deprecations are announced, GAIA creates tickets for each affected integration endpoint in your codebase, tagged with the deprecation deadline and migration guide link.

useCases.title: Churn event to Jira escalation
useCases.description: When a subscription cancellation cites a billing or product defect, GAIA identifies the corresponding open ticket and escalates its priority, attaching the churn event data as evidence.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Stripe to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Provide GAIA with a restricted, read-only Stripe API key and authenticate your Jira instance. Configure which event types and thresholds should trigger ticket creation.

howItWorks.step: Define revenue thresholds and ticket routing
howItWorks.description: Set the event conditions that warrant tickets, failure rates, MRR thresholds, specific error codes, and map them to projects, issue types, and priority levels.

howItWorks.step: GAIA monitors billing events and manages tickets automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA listens for the events you've configured and creates or updates tickets accordingly, annotating each with revenue context so your team can prioritize and resolve billing issues efficiently.

faqs.question: Does GAIA need write access to the Stripe account?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA uses read-only API access for monitoring events and subscription data. It never initiates charges, refunds, or any financial transactions.

faqs.question: Can GAIA distinguish between transient errors and systemic issues?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA applies configurable thresholds and time windows to distinguish a temporary gateway blip from a systemic billing failure. Only events exceeding your thresholds generate tickets.

faqs.question: Can GAIA correlate error spikes with recent Jira deployments?
faqs.answer: GAIA can correlate the timing of an error spike with recently completed tickets or sprint deployments, surfacing likely root cause candidates in the incident ticket.

faqs.question: What if a billing issue resolves before engineering investigates?
faqs.answer: GAIA monitors the event stream continuously. If an error condition clears, GAIA comments on the ticket noting the resolution and suggests closing or downgrading its priority.
